query: रासायनिक समीकरण को संतुलित करना क्यों आवश्यक है?
subject: Science
answer:
पाठ्यपुस्तक के आधार पर सटीक उत्तर:

कक्षा IX में आपने द्रव्यमान के संरक्षण के नियम का अध्ययन किया था; किसी भी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया में द्रव्यमान का न तो निर्माण होता है और न ही विनाश। अर्थात् किसी भी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के उत्पाद तत्वों का कुल द्रव्यमान अभिकारक तत्वों के कुल द्रव्यमान के बराबर होता है। दूसरे शब्दों में, रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के पहले एवं उसके पश्चात प्रत्येक तत्व के परमाणुओं की संख्या समान रहती है। इसलिए हमें कंकाली समीकरण को संतुलित करना आवश्यक होता है। उदाहरण: जिंक + सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल -> जिंक सल्फेट + हाइड्रोजन [Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2]। भाप के साथ लोहे की अभिक्रिया: 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2।

subject: Science
answer:
Textbook-verified answer:

Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the force acting on an object is directly proportional to the rate of change of linear momentum of the object and the change in momentum takes place in the direction of the force. Mathematical formulation: Let an object of mass m move with an initial velocity u along a straight line. If an external unbalanced force F acts on it for a duration of time t, its velocity changes to v. Initial momentum p1 = mu. Final momentum p2 = mv. Change in momentum Δp = mv - mu = m(v - u). Rate of change of momentum = Δp / t = m(v - u)/t = ma (since acceleration a = (v - u)/t). According to the law, F ∝ ma, so F = k * ma. In SI units, k = 1, hence F = m * a. Unit of force is Newton (N) in SI system and dyne in CGS system. 1 N = 10^5 dyne.

subject: Science
answer:
Textbook-verified answer:

Newton's First Law states that every body continues in its state of rest or in the state of uniform motion along a straight line unless it is acted upon by some external force. It defines force as well as inertia. Inertia is the inherent property of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or the state of uniform motion, unless it is influenced upon by an external unbalanced force. Types of Inertia: 1. Inertia of rest: The resistance of a body to change its state of rest (e.g., when a bus starts suddenly, passengers fall backwards). 2. Inertia of motion: The resistance of a body to change its state of motion (e.g., an athlete runs some distance before jumping). 3. Inertia of direction: The resistance of a body to change its direction of motion (e.g., when a vehicle takes a sharp turn, passengers lean outward).
